TABLE.NAME: local_elediaai_core_usage
TABLE.COMMENT: Per-user token quota counters for eLeDia.ai requests.

TABLE.NAME: local_elediaai_core_turn
TABLE.COMMENT: One row per AI turn of the suite: what was asked and answered, what it was grounded on, which feature asked and what it cost. Carries no user id by design (operator decision 05.09.2026); askerkey is a salted pseudonym that counts askers without naming one and makes an erasure request answerable.

FIELD.NAME: component
FIELD.COMMENT: Frankenstyle name of the feature that asked. The one thing Moodle's own ai_action_register cannot record.

FIELD.NAME: instanceid
FIELD.COMMENT: Placement instance id, 0 for a site-wide surface.

FIELD.NAME: actionname
FIELD.COMMENT: generate_text, summarise_text, explain_text, generate_image or chat_turn.

FIELD.NAME: courseid
FIELD.COMMENT: Derived from contextid at write time so the course report does not walk the context tree once per row.

FIELD.NAME: askerkey
FIELD.COMMENT: sha256 of the user id plus a site salt. Never displayed, never resolved by any surface; empty string when no person was involved.

FIELD.NAME: origin
FIELD.COMMENT: grounded (answered from indexed course material), general (from the model) or mcp (read out of Moodle through a tool).

FIELD.NAME: topic
FIELD.COMMENT: Canonical topic label from the backend, when it supplies one.

FIELD.NAME: sourcetitle
FIELD.COMMENT: Title of the primary cited source.

FIELD.NAME: cmid
FIELD.COMMENT: Course module of the primary cited source, when resolvable. No foreign key: a deleted module must not take the row with it.

FIELD.NAME: tokensestimated
FIELD.COMMENT: Whether the two token counts are an estimate rather than the backend's own figure. The chat backends do not all report usage; the credit chokepoint then books an estimate, and the log has to say which of the two a reader is looking at.

FIELD.NAME: registerid
FIELD.COMMENT: The row this request produced in Moodle's own ai_action_register, when it went through core_ai. Lets the register view leave out what the suite already lists itself. Null for chat turns: they reach their backend on their own transport and never touch that register.

TABLE.NAME: local_elediaai_core_action
TABLE.COMMENT: One row per action the AI performed through a tool on somebody's behalf: which tool, whether it changed anything, and who it acted for. Keeps the person on purpose -- oversight without an actor is not oversight. Holds no content; that is the turn log's job. A projection of the tool events, not a second log: the event store keeps them too, but encodes its payload as JSON or PHP-serialised depending on configuration and is therefore not queryable.

FIELD.NAME: userid
FIELD.COMMENT: Who the AI acted for. Set to 0 by the retention task; the row itself is kept, because a proof that disappears on request is not one.

FIELD.NAME: component
FIELD.COMMENT: Frankenstyle of the plugin that owns the tool.

FIELD.NAME: toolname
FIELD.COMMENT: The tool as the agent called it, e.g. moodle_grade_submission.

FIELD.NAME: iswrite
FIELD.COMMENT: Whether the tool changed state. Taken from the tool's own MCP annotations, not guessed from its name.

FIELD.NAME: turnid
FIELD.COMMENT: The turn that caused this action. Prepared but always null: the MCP token is issued per user, not per turn, so nothing links the two yet.
